To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cl transport at cerebrovascular endothelial cells and choroid plexuses is a saturable, concentration‐dependent process.
chloride is transported from blood to brain by a saturable, concentration‐dependent process at both the cerebrovascular epithelium and the choroid plesus epithelium.
Cl transport across the blood‐brain barrier is a saturable process, with a Km for Cl of approximately 60 μmol × ml-1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method of treatment for the control of the blood pressure in hypertension, which is based on the discovery of a new mechanism for the regulation of blood pressure.
the development of new and more efficient catalysts based on metal oxides and metal oxide supported metal catalysts.
the transport of Cl across the blood‐brain barrier.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cl transport at cerebrovascular endothelial cells is a saturable carrier‐mediated process that is dependent on plasma Cl concentration.
the blood–brain barrier (BBB) is not a barrier to chloride.
the brain‐blood barrier is not an impenetrable wall but a selective permeability system that is subject to modulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transport of Cl at the blood‐brain barrier is carrier‐mediated, saturable and concentration‐dependent.

Cl is transported across the blood‐brain barrier by a system that is similar to the Na/K/2Cl cotransport system in renal tubular epithelium, with the exception that the carrier in brain is not inhibited by furosemide.

Cl transport at both the choroid plesus epithelium and the cerebrovascular endotelia is a saturable, concentration‐dependent process and that the choroid plessus epithelium plays a major role in the regulation of Cl concentration in CSF and brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chloride can enter the brain through the choroid plessus epithelium, which is the barrier between the blood and the cerebrospinal (CSF) fluid.
Cl transport at both the blood‐brain and blood‐CSF barriers is a saturable process.
the blood–brain barrier (BBB) is a dynamic structure that allows for the passage of substances into and out of the brain, and that this passage is not always passive.
